solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: State benefit is about right (6)

indicatorNotes.is about: 'about' means surrounding, so the benefit word wraps around the R

blocks.note: an asset is something of benefit

annotation.surface: A sour remark that welfare payments are mostly about what you're entitled to.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State benefit' reads as one welfare phrase; split it, and 'State' is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to state a claim is to put it forward firmly as true.

entries.clue: Request job is not started (3)

indicatorNotes.is not started: something not started has had its beginning left off, so the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: TASK without its first letter T

annotation.surface: Someone asks for work to be done that nobody has begun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Request' can be a noun or a verb; the clue needs the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to put in a request for something.

entries.clue: Tool I lost from small basket on bicycle (7)

indicatorNotes.lost from: what is lost from something is no longer in it, so the I drops out of the basket word

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
a pannier is a bag or basket slung on a bike

annotation.surface: A cyclist has lost a tool out of the little basket on the bike.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a cyclist's toolkit, which is exactly where the answer would be found.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the British spanner is the tool Americans call a wrench.

entries.clue: Restoration of controls on gallery male staff beginning to thieve (13)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so take only the T of 'thieve'

blocks.note: the reins are the controls, as in 'take the reins'
the Tate is the London art gallery
staff who are male are men

annotation.surface: Security at an art gallery is being tightened after men on the staff started stealing.
annotation.walkthrough: The Tate is London's national gallery of British and modern art, and a crossword's default 'gallery'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: restoring someone to a post or a rule to force is reinstating it.

entries.clue: To walk around a bit in shoes (6)

indicatorNotes.around: to turn around is to face the other way, so the walk word is written backwards

annotation.surface: An invitation to stroll about for a while in your shoes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A bit in shoes' reads as 'for a while'; it is the definition, a part of a shoe.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the reinforced front of a boot or shoe is one bit of it.

entries.clue: Sight loon trio? That might have me excited (13)

annotation.definition: Sight loon trio? That might have me excited

indicatorNotes.excited: excited things are stirred up, so the letters are too

annotation.surface: A birdwatcher says spotting three loons would get them worked up.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the 'me' who would be thrilled to see three loons is a bird expert. A loon is a diver, a water bird, not a fool.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes a bird scientist's delight at a rare sighting, which is who the answer is.

entries.clue: Canine clubs Igor’s running (5)

indicatorNotes.running: things running are on the move, so Igor's letters shift about

annotation.surface: Igor is running a dog club.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Canine' reads as an adjective describing clubs; it is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the short-legged Welsh herding breed is one kind of canine.

entries.clue: Gradual cessation of war reportedly upset male (9)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a word that sounds like the one meant
indicatorNotes.upset: something upset is knocked over, so MALE's letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: peace ends a war; PIECE sounds the same

annotation.surface: A man is unhappy that the war is winding down only slowly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gradual cessation of war' reads as one phrase; only 'Gradual' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: done a bit at a time rather than all at once.

entries.clue: Initially Kitchener has a kit inspection so some uniforms appear (5)

annotation.definitionNote: the answer names the cloth and colour of such uniforms

indicatorNotes.Initially: initially means at the start, so take the first letter of each word that follows

blocks.clueFragment: Initially Kitchener has a kit inspection
blocks.note: first letters of Kitchener, has, a, kit, inspection

annotation.surface: Lord Kitchener holds a kit inspection and the soldiers turn up in uniform.
annotation.walkthrough: Kitchener was the British field marshal of the First World War recruiting poster, which suits an army answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by metonymy: the dull brown-green cloth stands for the army uniforms made from it.

entries.clue: Disconcert gunners over abandoning all cover (7)

indicatorNotes.abandoning all cover: a word's cover is its outside letters, and 'all' means both words shed theirs

blocks.note: GUNNERS without its first and last letters
OVER without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Artillerymen are rattled when they have to leave all their shelter behind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gunners' tempts you to write RA, the Royal Artillery; here the word itself is stripped.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to rattle someone and take away their composure.

entries.clue: Unpleasant to see guy left distraught (4)

indicatorNotes.distraught: someone distraught is in a state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

annotation.surface: It is a grim sight when a man is left in distress.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as abandoned; it only supplies the L for the mix.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: displeasing to the eye.

entries.clue: Manage to get uniform in Royal Navy (3)

indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another sits inside it, so U goes inside RN

blocks.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A sailor contrives to be issued a uniform in the Royal Navy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Manage to get' reads as 'contrive'; only 'Manage' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be in charge of a business or project.

entries.clue: Journey using cycle before start of fall? (5,4)

indicatorNotes.before: what comes before is placed first, so the cycle word leads

blocks.note: a round is a cycle, as in a round of talks
a stumble is how a fall begins

annotation.surface: A bike ride taken just as autumn begins.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Start of fall' looks like an instruction to take F; the question mark flags a cryptic hint instead: a fall starts with a stumble.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: an outward and return journey together.

entries.clue: Gem of a game (9)

blocks.note: a single diamond set on its own
a game played by one person, with cards or pegs

annotation.surface: Praise for an excellent game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gem of a game' is a compliment; split it, and both nouns are definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of being alone: a stone set by itself, and a game for one player.

entries.clue: Commotion raised by one who rows on river (6)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so OAR follows R

blocks.note: an oar is a rower, as in 'a good oar'

annotation.surface: A fuss started by a rower on the river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One who rows' is a person, but crosswords use the oar itself for the rower.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a noisy public disturbance or outcry.

entries.clue: A learner taking on additional confidence (6)

indicatorNotes.taking on: to take something on is to take it aboard, so the extra word holds A and L inside

blocks.note: L = learner, from the L-plate on a learner's car

annotation.surface: A learner driver gains extra self-belief.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taking on additional' reads as gaining more; the verb is the container.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the spirit and self-belief of a person or group.

entries.clue: Fuss over point editor took up (7)

annotation.surface: An editor made a fuss about a point and took it up.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts ADO above the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: past tense of taking on an idea or cause as your own.

entries.clue: Hold back, needing time for one old engineer (4)

indicatorNotes.needing time for one: one thing 'for' another stands in its place, so T takes the place of I

blocks.note: to wait is to hold back
I = one, the Roman numeral, which T replaces

annotation.surface: An old engineer must hang back and take his time.
annotation.walkthrough: James Watt was the 18th-century Scottish engineer of the steam engine.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Scot whose steam-engine work gave his name to the unit of power.

entries.clue: Outlaw road speed changes (9)

indicatorNotes.changes: a thing that changes takes a new form, so the letters take a new order

annotation.surface: A proposal to ban changes to road speed limits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' reads as a verb, to ban; it is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a reckless Wild West bandit is one kind of outlaw.

entries.clue: Receive following second post (5)

indicatorNotes.following: what follows comes after, so the receive word comes after S

annotation.surface: Someone gets the next batch of mail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second post' reads as the later mail delivery; 'post' is a wooden pole.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a pointed pole driven into the ground.

entries.clue: Hunting bird’s cry heard in east London (3)

indicatorNotes.heard in east London: the Cockney accent of east London drops the H, so the word is written as a Cockney would say it

annotation.surface: The call of a bird of prey is heard in the East End.
annotation.walkthrough: Cockneys, from east London, are famous for dropping their Hs.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the nocturnal raptor that hunts mice and voles.

entries.clue: Cause of chemical change damaged a green tree at first (7)

indicatorNotes.damaged: something damaged is broken up, so the letters are too
indicatorNotes.at first: at first means at the start, so take only the T of 'tree'

annotation.surface: A chemical has harmed a green tree.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a chemical spill, and the answer is the very substance that did it.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a substance added to bring about a chemical reaction.

entries.clue: Bury losing the first of season (5)

indicatorNotes.losing the first: to lose the first is to be without the opening letter, so the W goes

annotation.surface: Bury, the English football club, has lost the opening match of the season.
annotation.walkthrough: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester with a football club; the capital is only there to disguise the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to place a dead body in a grave.

entries.clue: Fish that’s regularly greasy (3)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so take every other letter

annotation.surface: A fish that is always oily.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' reads as 'always'; it picks every second letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the flat, winged sea fish related to sharks and skates.

entries.clue: Rather small-minded welcoming king (6)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the small-minded word takes in R

annotation.surface: A grudging remark that someone was petty in the way they received the king.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rather' looks like it qualifies 'small-minded'; it is the definition, as in 'pretty good'.
annotation.definitionFit: An adverb synonym: 'fairly' or 'quite', as in a tiring day that leaves you rather worn out.

entries.clue: Dog breaking in where pigs are heavy to eat (6)

indicatorNotes.breaking: what is broken falls apart, so DOG's letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.in: breaking in means entering, so the rearranged dog goes inside the pigs' home

annotation.surface: A dog breaks into a pigsty where the swill is thick and filling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Breaking in' does double duty: 'breaking' mixes the dog, and 'in' puts it inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Describes food like suet pudding that sits heavily in the stomach.
